summary: On a fast day for rain, everyone gathers in the town square and puts ashes on their heads. The oldest one reminds them that Hashem wants teshuvah, not only fasting.

summary: Kohanim who serve in the Beis HaMikdash must not drink wine when they might be needed for the avodah. During their week they may not cut their hair or wash clothes, except on Thursday for Shabbos.
stIntro: The mishna mentions another difference between the members of the priestly watch and the patrilineal family:

chunks.en: The men of the mishmar may drink wine at night,
chunks.st: The members of the priestly watch were permitted to drink wine during the nights,

chunks.en: but not in the daytime.
chunks.explain: In the daytime they might be called to help with the avodah.
chunks.st: but not during the days,
chunks.stMore: as they might be called upon to assist in the Temple service, which may not be performed after drinking wine.

chunks.en: But the men of the beis av,
chunks.st: And the members of the patrilineal family,
chunks.stMore: who performed the Temple service, were not permitted to drink wine,

chunks.en: not by day and not at night.

summary: The community's fasts do not begin on a Thursday, so that prices will not go up. The sets of fasts go Monday, Thursday, Monday, or Thursday, Monday, Thursday.

chunks.st: the community starting on a Thursday,

chunks.en: so as not to make prices go up.
chunks.explain: Everyone would shop on Friday, and sellers would raise their prices.
chunks.st: so as not to cause an increase in prices.
chunks.stMore: If the first of a series of fasts is on a Thursday, then on Friday everyone will come to purchase their food for after the fast and for Shabbat, which will allow the storeowners to take advantage of the crowds and raise their prices.

chunks.en: Rather, the first three fasts are
